key_insight: A phononic subsurface embedded in a flat plate can passively reshape sustained vortex shedding, with its position and resonant growth rate determining whether lift and drag oscillations are amplified or strongly damped.
engineering_relevance: By tuning where the subsurface sits and how it resonates, engineers may reduce unsteady loading on bluff or separated-flow surfaces with minimal impact on mean forces.
method: High-fidelity immersed boundary simulation of strongly coupled fluid-structure interaction.
Flat-plate flow with fully separated, periodic vortex shedding and an embedded grounded diatomic-chain phononic subsurface.
Parameter study over subsurface chordwise position and resonant displacement-amplitude growth rate.
evidence_signal: The simulations identified four position-dependent limit-cycle regimes and a configuration that cut lift oscillation amplitude by over 30% and drag oscillation amplitude by over 50% with less than 0.5% change in mean lift and drag.
watch_item: The reported benefits come from a specific idealized separated-flow configuration and may shift with Reynolds number, geometry, or structural/material realizability.
paper_title: Interaction of Sustained Vortex Shedding with a Phononic Subsurface: Effect of Positioning and Resonant Characteristics
